text: On the cosmos_qa testbed, we evaluated weak-to-strong generalization using a method that trains only a linear head on frozen strong-model features, with a probe learning rate of 0.001. Across 3 seeds, the measured performance gap recovered (PGR) was 0.28. No baseline PGR was provided for this configuration, so this number cannot be interpreted as an improvement over any alternative method; it stands only as a standalone measurement of how much of the gap between the weak supervisor and the strong ceiling this linear-probe setup recovers. The sample of 3 seeds is small, and no standard error or seed-level spread was reported, so the run-to-run variability of this estimate is unknown and the value of 0.28 should be treated as provisional. Further seeds, a reported variance estimate, and a matched baseline would be needed before drawing comparative conclusions about whether frozen-feature linear probing is competitive with full fine-tuning approaches on this task.
